english.title: Designer / manufacturer etc fail provide revised info about use for which article was designed / tested

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Health and Safety at Work Act 1974

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the

(A)_[designer]_
(B)_[manufacturer]_
(C)_[importer]_
(D)_[supplier]_

of an article

(E)_[for use at work,]_
(F)_[of fairground equipment,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY ARTICLE..), failed to discharge your duty to take such steps as were necessary to secure, so far as was reasonably practicable, that persons supplied by you with that article were provided with all such revisions of information provided to them by virtue of section 6(1)(c) of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974 as were necessary by reason of its becoming known that something gave rise to a serious risk to health or safety
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 6(1)(d) and 33(1)(a)of, and Schedule 3A to, the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
designer / manufacturer / importer / supplier of article
for use at work / fairground equipment
fail to take steps necessary to secure that persons supplied
were provided with revision of info about use for which it was designed / tested
and about conditions necessary to ensure safe when use / cleaning / maintenance / dismantling / disposal
knowing that something gave rise to serious risk to health or safety

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 2(2) of the Act for examples of the extent of the employer's duty.
(ii) Proceedings for an offence shall not, in England and Wales, be instituted except by an inspector of the Environment Agency or the Natural Resources Body for Wales or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions, see section 38 of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2002; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see schedule 3A to the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
